wy_walt_s_wall.blurb: A classic old-school wall in the Vedauwoo area between Laramie and Cheyenne, sitting at the south end of the Turtle Rock group and a short walk from the lot below the campground. Most of the 27 climbs here are trad, mainly cracks and slabs that run from easy scrambles up to hard 5.12, with a handful of bolted lines and a few boulder problems from V3 to V10. The granite is rough on the hands, though decades of traffic have taken the edge off the popular lines. Because the face bakes in the sun for much of the day, early starts are the norm. Easy multi-pitch routes make it a common first outing at Vedauwoo, and the main descent is by rappel, which can back up on busy days.

wy_superratic_pillar.blurb: A steep, clean panel on the far side of the Valhalla zone in upper Ten Sleep Canyon, about a quarter mile along the trail past the main Valhalla walls. All 27 routes are bolted sport lines, and the grade range starts around 5.9 but the real weight sits higher: roughly sixteen routes fall in the 5.12 to 5.13 range, with a few more above that. Only a handful of 5.10 and 5.11 lines exist, so this is not the place for a warm-up day or a newer leader. Lines are vertical to overhanging on very good stone, and the pillar is home to a couple of the canyon's best-known hard routes.

wy_worm_drive.blurb: A small, quiet formation tucked away in the Vedauwoo country west of Laramie, reached by a drive down a forest track and a walk along a creek. Most of the 27 climbs are short trad lines, many of them cracks and offwidths, with a few bolted sport routes and some boulder problems, spanning easy 5th class up to the 5.11 range and a couple of harder problems. Expect solitude rather than crowds, a rough granite surface, and a need for wide gear if you want the signature cracks. The area is known for hard wide-crack climbing, and few of the obvious lines have been recorded in detail.
wy_worm_drive.parking_note: Drive the forest road that leaves the main Vedauwoo road and drops down to a turnaround beside a stream; leave the car there. The trail to the crag starts on the far side of the water.
wy_worm_drive.approach: Cross the stream on the fallen logs, then follow the clear trail along the creek for roughly half a mile. At the first clearing, turn left over a low hill; the small formation sits on its eastern edge.

wy_sanctuary_the.blurb: A cliff high in Sinks Canyon above the waterfall trail near Lander, directly under the larger Granite Buttress. It feels wilder and more alpine than the limestone walls lower in the canyon. Of the 26 routes, 21 are sport and five are trad, mostly on gently overhanging, good-quality stone with technical, reachy movement. The grades start near 5.8 but cluster in the 5.11 to 5.12 range, with a few 5.13s and one harder line, so it suits solid intermediates and up. The wall is sheltered, which helps on breezy days. Watch for snakes and poison ivy in warm months.

wy_2_spooky_tooth_area.blurb: A cluster of short sport routes on the western end of Fairfield Hill in Sinks Canyon near Lander, named for the tall flake leaning against the wall. All 26 routes are bolted, ranging from friendly 5.6 and 5.7 lines through a middle band of 5.10s up to 5.13, with the biggest group at 5.12. Climbs are short and often punchy, and the cliff carries striking orange and black streaks. A cluster of animal-themed lines sits on top of a small hummock nearby. The approach is a steep haul up from the road, so the area tends to be quieter than the main limestone wall.

wy_a_west_sector.blurb: The farthest-left section of Rock Springs Buttress, a high alpine-style cliff just south of Jackson Hole Mountain Resort, with a steep gully bounding it on one side. It is reached either by the long hike up from the ski area or by dropping down from the top of the tram, and it is the first wall you meet from above. Most of the 26 climbs are multi-pitch alpine-flavored lines, with a few sport and trad routes and a single boulder problem. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.13, with the largest group at 5.11. The rock is fractured and weathered, so wear a helmet. Mornings are shady and cool, with sun arriving later in the day.
